results.summary_before: This design implements a lightweight Trivium stream cipher variant using three 64-bit shift registers to generate a keystream that is XORed with input data for encryption and decryption. It uses 8-bit data and control inputs via the input and bidirectional pins, and outputs an 8-bit stream on the output pins. The design is fully self-contained and is tested only in simulation using Verilog or Cocotb testbenches, with no external hardware required. It is notable for being a compact hardware implementation of a cryptographic primitive suitable for Tiny Tapeout.

results.summary_before: This project is a TV-B-Gone device that sends infrared codes to turn off many European TVs, either in a continuous loop or once per button press. It uses an external IR LED connected through a transistor for higher current, and status LEDs indicate active and failure states. The design requires an 8 MHz clock, which can be generated by an RPi Pico, and an optional start button. Silicon tests show it successfully turned off a TV, but it needed a manual reset and the start signal is active low, requiring a pull-up.

results.summary_before: This project implements a weighted majority voter and trend detector that observes a stream of binary input bits over a configurable sliding window, weighting more recent bits more heavily. The weighted sum is compared against upper and lower thresholds with hysteresis, so the output holds its state between thresholds and only changes on sustained input trends, acting as a debouncer and noise filter. It is fully digital and synchronous, requiring no external hardware beyond an optional LED or logic analyzer on the output, and can be simulated with the provided Verilog testbench or cocotb test. The documentation is detailed but reports no silicon test results.

results.summary_before: OctoPWM is an eight-channel PWM driver controlled over SPI, with each channel having a 10-bit compare threshold and a shared configurable clock divider. It accepts 16-bit SPI transactions with a write address and value, uses active-low chip select and enable pins, and outputs eight PWM signals plus a divided clock output. The design targets a 10 MHz clock, matches the Tiny Tapeout audio pinout, and needs no external hardware beyond the SPI host. The author notes it was made in one night with no prior HDL experience and that the testbench is lacking, so correct operation is hoped for rather than fully verified.

results.summary_before: This is a test project synthesized with Dyno-SV, a new open-source synthesis tool, to gate level using the SkyWater 130nm standard cell library. The design finds the indices of the first, second, and third set bits in an 8-bit input word and outputs their positions along with valid flags. It also includes a counter and configuration bits to select registered or combinational input and output paths. The project serves as a validation of the Dyno-SV synthesis flow and requires no external hardware.

results.summary_before: This design implements a Morse code transmitter and receiver using two finite state machines to encode and decode Morse sequences for alphabets and digits. It accepts button inputs for dots, dashes, and spaces, and outputs decoded ASCII characters. The design is intended for testing with an FPGA board and a 16x2 LCD for display. It is a straightforward educational project for learning Morse code and FSM design.
